chunks: Those who do not believe, say: 'When we and our fathers have turned to dust, how shall we be raised again?'
ai.seo_question: What is the disbelievers' argument against resurrection in Surah An-Naml?
ai.summary: In Surah An-Naml, this verse captures the core objection of the disbelievers who reduce resurrection to a physical impossibility, arguing that once bodies and ancestors have turned to dust, reassembly is beyond nature's capacity. Shia exegetes, such as Allamah Tabatabai in *Al-Mizan*, emphasize that this skepticism stems from a materialistic worldview that ignores God's power to recreate what He originally formed, linking this doubt to the broader theme of *Ma'ad* (resurrection) as a logical necessity of divine omnipotence rather than a mere physical miracle.
